pillars.name: family
pillars.title: Family
pillars.description: The first sphere of Ubuntu — the household and kin who form a person's primary web of belonging. Ubuntu begins here: identity is given by family before it is given by any institution.

pillars.name: community
pillars.title: Community
pillars.description: The extended sphere of neighbours, peers, and chosen kin. Where the family ends, the community begins; the two are continuous, not opposed. Ubuntu treats community as the medium through which a person grows into society.

pillars.name: society
pillars.title: Society
pillars.description: The broader human web — strangers, institutions, the polity. Ubuntu does not stop at the village wall; vanhu means people, all people. A person who treats strangers as strangers has not yet practised Ubuntu.

pillars.name: environment
pillars.title: Environment
pillars.description: The natural world that holds all relationships. Ubuntu is ecological before it is social — soil, water, and weather are kin too. A person who exhausts the environment has broken Ubuntu, even if they have wronged no human directly.

pillars.name: spirituality
pillars.title: Spirituality
pillars.description: The vertical axis of being human — meaning, purpose, ancestry, and the sacred. Unhu names the inner quality from which Ubuntu flows outward. Without unhu, the four horizontal pillars are scaffolding without a soul.

principles.name: survival
principles.title: Survival
principles.description: Collective endurance. No one survives alone; basic needs are met through one another. Reciprocal care sustains the community before any individual can flourish.

principles.name: solidarity
principles.title: Solidarity
principles.description: A firm and persevering commitment to the common good. Not vague compassion but active allegiance to the welfare of the whole — kubatana means to hold together.

principles.name: compassion
principles.title: Compassion
principles.description: Active care, sympathy, and concern shown through helping, sharing, and welcoming. Tsitsi extends beyond kin to all — a stranger in need is not a stranger to compassion. (Also: Du Toit, Poovan & Engelbretch 2006.)

principles.name: respect
principles.title: Respect
principles.description: Unprejudiced consideration of another's privileges, beliefs, and norms. Encompasses elder-respect (ukuhlonipha) but applies to every person, every age, every belief. (Also: Poovan et al. 2006.)

principles.name: dignity
principles.title: Dignity
principles.description: Inherent worth held by virtue of existence — irrespective of status, ethnicity, age, or background. Humanity is sacred. Dignity is not earned and cannot be revoked. (Also: Ramose 2002.)

constraints.name: outdoor-readability
constraints.title: Outdoor readability
constraints.description: Every surface is read in direct sunlight on a budget phone, not only at a desk.

constraints.name: connectivity-gradient-design
constraints.title: Connectivity-gradient design
constraints.description: Design for the whole range of connections, from none to fibre. Offline-first is the enforced minimum: core tasks work with no connection, and better connectivity adds to that baseline.

constraints.name: multilingual-parity
constraints.title: Multilingual parity
constraints.description: Shona, Ndebele and English are equal. No language is a translation of another, and none ships later.

constraints.name: shared-device-awareness
constraints.title: Shared-device awareness
constraints.description: One phone often serves a household. A person's data belongs to that person, not to the device.

constraints.name: personal-data-sovereignty
constraints.title: Personal data sovereignty
constraints.description: A person owns their data. It lives on their device first, syncs to their own isolated cloud space, and moves to pods in the Nyuchi Honeycomb without being reshaped.

constraints.name: no-surveillance-business-model
constraints.title: No surveillance business model
constraints.description: We do not earn money from attention or personal data.

constraints.name: bundu-floor
constraints.title: The Bundu floor
constraints.description: The minimums nothing can go under: text size, contrast, hit regions and spacing, so that nobody is punished for their eyesight or their device.
